Source inspection of npm tarballs. react-native-video 6.19.3 Android ReactExoplayerView.onMetadata maps only Id3Frame and EventMessage and logs 'unhandled metadata' for other entries (Media3 IcyInfo), so ICY StreamTitle is dropped on Android; iOS RCTPlayerObserver uses AVPlayerItemMetadataOutput and forwards timed metadata groups via onTimedMetadata. expo-audio 58.0.11 has no timed/ICY metadata API (metadata only for lock-screen display). react-native-track-player 4.1.2 exposes AudioMetadataReceived/MetadataTimedReceived/MetadataCommonReceived events (native via kotlinaudio v2.1.0 and SwiftAudioEx).

expo-audio docs (expo/expo docs/pages/versions/unversioned/sdk/audio.mdx): enableBackgroundPlayback config plugin adds Android mediaPlayback foreground service and iOS audio background mode; setActiveForLockScreen required on Android for sustained background playback (otherwise stops after ~3 min). react-native-video 6.19.3 has playInBackground and showNotificationControls props (Android MediaSession notification, iOS NowPlayingInfoCenterManager).

results.title: GDPR and serving to the EU

evidence.summary: IP addresses are personal data under GDPR; the app causes the device IP to be sent to Radio Browser servers (click counting by IP) and to arbitrary broadcaster stream servers worldwide. Need a privacy notice naming these recipients, no tracking SDKs to stay out of ePrivacy consent, and favicon/logo loading also leaks IP to station hosts.

evidence.query: Warner Music v TuneIn Court of Appeal ruling linking radio streams communication to the public EU copyright radio aggregator app
evidence.summary: TuneIn v Warner [2021] EWCA Civ 441 (UK court applying CJEU communication-to-the-public case law: Svensson, GS Media, VG Bild-Kunst): an aggregator linking users to foreign radio streams not licensed in the territory infringed copyright (new public). Relevant copyright risk for an EU-targeted radio directory app; geo-relevant station filtering and takedown process advisable.

No server to run. Operational dependencies: Radio Browser community servers (volunteer-run, availability/SLA unknown, must resolve server list at runtime and send a descriptive User-Agent per community practice - unverified first-party); station stream URLs and favicons go stale; react-native-video v6 is maintained but on interop layer with v7 (Nitro) next, so plan a migration; patch-package patch for Android ICY must be re-applied on every RNV upgrade. Signal for monitoring: crash/ANR reporting would add a third-party SDK (privacy trade-off).

Many radio streams are plain http: iOS ATS needs NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsForMedia (narrower than NSAllowsArbitraryLoads) and Android needs a network security config permitting cleartext for media only; App Review may ask for justification. All directory data (names, URLs, favicons) and ICY StreamTitle strings are untrusted third-party input: render as plain text, length-limit, never open as deep links automatically. Supply chain: pin exact versions with lockfile; commercial license change in RNTP main shows upstream license can change between versions, so pin and re-check on upgrade.

decision.rationale: Maintained MIT player on Media3 ExoPlayer and AVPlayer that plays HLS and progressive MP3/AAC live streams out of the box; one native dependency also covers background/notification controls and timed metadata. Tool hint is extend only because metrics are missing (GitHub anon core quota 0/60, api.npmjs.org blocked); manual checks ev_0885f3d682e5 confirm MIT LICENSE (master and 6.19.3 tarball), release 2026-09-18 and v6 status 'Maintained, New Arch via interop'. Pin 6.19.3; plan move to v7 (Nitro, MIT) once stable.

alternatives.why_not: Only 4.1.2 is Apache-2.0; the v4 branch is frozen (no further updates) and is a legacy native module running on the New Architecture only through interop, risky for future RN and Android target-SDK bumps. Main branch/v5 is commercially licensed.
RNTP v5 under a custom commercial license (license.txt): any non-personal/non-educational use needs a paid license with no-redistribution terms; price not verifiable (rntp.dev blocked).
Good audio-first player with lock-screen controls, but exposes no timed/ICY metadata, so feature 4 would require building a native module on both platforms.
Low-level Web Audio engine with FFmpeg-based streamer; no ICY metadata and far heavier than a radio player needs.

component.name: stream-playback
component.description: Play live internet radio streams (HLS, MP3, AAC/Icecast/Shoutcast) on Android and iOS from React Native.

decision.rationale: Use react-native-video onTimedMetadata. iOS already forwards AVPlayerItemMetadataOutput timed metadata (ICY StreamTitle); Android ReactExoplayerView.onMetadata drops Media3 IcyInfo ('unhandled metadata'), so add a few-line patch-package patch mapping IcyInfo.title to a TimedMetadata entry (and consider upstreaming). HLS now-playing via ID3 already works on Android.

alternatives.why_not: Emits ICY metadata on both platforms out of the box, but rejected as the player (frozen v4, commercial v5); not worth a second player.
JS parser needs a second HTTP connection with a streaming response body (not supported by RN fetch) and doubles bandwidth; reference for the format only.
LGPL-3.0-or-later and browser/MSE oriented; not usable inside native players.
2-star JS parser with the same second-connection problem; license not verified by the tool.
